text:
nora: ran a short-run replay of the micro-chat profile on staging. host ingress CPU dominated by tokenization + many tiny grpc writes. baseline sample attached.

lee: can you paste the sample hotspots?

nora: top spots from pprof: 
``n  51.2%  ingress_worker  tokenize::sanitize_and_split
  23.7%  ingress_worker  grpc::writev_small
   7.9%  ingress_worker  kvcache::fetch_remote
   4.6%  ingress_worker  http::frame_pack
```

pablo: that tokenize number is brutal. is gateway pretokenizing?

nora: yes, gateway does optimistic pretokenize for some clients but host still runs sanitize for stream-attach fallbacks. we can add a restrictive header to skip sanitize for internal tenants: `X-Token-Skip: 1`.

jess: low risk for internal traffic, but we should keep a fallback when clients omit header. add a fast safety-check on host that verifies minimal invariants before skipping.

lee: writev_small storms look like many 256B fragments. current coalesce window is 1ms. can we do adaptive coalescing instead of a fixed bump?

nora: i ran a sim: bumping to 6ms across-the-board cuts write syscalls 40% but adds ~5ms median for tiny requests. adaptive seems nicer: only enable larger window if worker sees sustained small-write rate.

pablo: implement a leaky-bucket detector: if small_write_count/sec > THRESH then enable coalesce for TTL ms. revert when rate subsides. track metrics: small_write_rate, coalesce_on, avg_syscalls_per_req.

jess: agree. also kernel-selector note: some kernels prioritized single-request latency and disable the merged-write path. we should add a kernel score component for "host-batching-friendly" so selector prefers kernels that keep write coalescing codepaths enabled under short-request workloads.

lee: selector currently uses latency and throughput heuristics. add a host_syscall_penalty computed from recent ingress flame histograms (tokenize% and writev%). bias selection when recent p50 < 80ms and p95 < 300ms (i.e., short-request regime).

pablo: kvcache: repeated prefix lookups show up despite overall low %; for tiny requests the absolute cost matters. propose a tiny per-worker direct memo: 256-entry LRU keyed by prefix-hash with 8s TTL. feature-flagged.

jess: watch memory and correctness. add eviction-on-memory-pressure and track mem_usage, hit_rate, miss_latency.

nora: proposed TODOs:
- header gate `X-Token-Skip` for internal tenants + fast invariant check (nora)
- adaptive small-write coalesce detector (lee)
- per-worker prefix memo LRU (pablo)
- kernel-selector policy: add host_syscall_penalty and seq-hist classifier (jess + lee)

pablo: i'll prototype the LRU with 256 entries, measure hit-rate on replay, and open a feature-flag PR.

jess: i'll draft kernel-selector changes and a simple classifier that uses p10/p50/p95 token lengths over a sliding 1min window.

lee: i'll implement detector: threshold tunables [200,500,1000], coalesce window options [4ms,6ms,10ms], and TTL 10s. will add dashboard panels: small_write_rate, coalesce_active, p50_latency_delta.

diag-bot: note: canary slots free: 4 and 6. recommend canary for header-gate once tests pass.

nora: timeline: header gate PR today, canary tomorrow. detector + LRU in parallel next 48h. include pre/post flamegraphs in PRs and assert tokenize% drops >= 25% for short-workload.

jess: also add automated perf-runner check: writev_syscalls/sec decrease > 30% or p50 latency delta < +6ms.

pablo: thanks — i'll share replay data and mem-profile attachments on the PR.

lee: sounds good. let's keep this lightweight and gated. will coordinate canary slots. :thumbsup:
